record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: What is the precise theoretical connection between the observed broadening or melting of the ρ meson in hot hadronic matter and chiral symmetry restoration in the quark-gluon plasma, and can missing LHC, intermediate-mass, and small-system dilepton data determine whether collective features in small systems accompany hot-matter formation?

evidence.quote: The connection between the observed broadening of the ρ in hot hadronic matter and chiral symmetry restoration in the QGP is however still more of a conjecture than a solid theoretical derivation.

On the experimental side, precision results from LHC are still missing, and may have to wait a few years for detector upgrades. Likewise needed is better data on the intermediate mass region (thermal radiation, charm) from both RHIC and LHC, and ideally even in pp/pA to see if the collective features observed in small systems go hand in hand with "hot matter".

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a strongly interacting medium described by finite-temperature QCD with light quark flavors. In the hadronic phase, the ρ meson has a vector-current spectral function ρ_V(q_0, q; T, μ_B) that, in equilibrium at temperature T and baryon chemical potential μ_B, governs the thermal dilepton emission rate

  dN_{ℓ⁺ℓ⁻}/d⁴q d⁴x = -(α²/(π³ M²)) f_B(q_0; T) Im Π_V(q_0, q; T, μ_B),

where Im Π_V is proportional to ρ_V, M² = q_0² - |q|², and f_B is the Bose distribution. Empirically, ρ_V exhibits a strong broadening ("melting") as T approaches the pseudocritical temperature T_pc ≈ 155 MeV. Chiral symmetry restoration is characterized by the degeneracy of the vector and axial-vector spectral functions, ρ_V(q_0, q; T) → ρ_A(q_0, q; T), as encoded by the Weinberg-type sum rules

  ∫_0^∞ (ds/s) [ρ_V(s; T) - ρ_A(s; T)] = f_π(T)² / something,
  ∫_0^∞ ds [ρ_V(s; T) - ρ_A(s; T)] = f_π(T)²,
  ∫_0^∞ ds · s · [ρ_V(s; T) - ρ_A(s; T)] = -2π α_s ⟨(q̄q)²⟩(T) (up to standard coefficients),

with chiral order parameters such as the quark condensate ⟨q̄q⟩(T) and the pion decay constant f_π(T).

Provide a rigorous theoretical derivation, starting from the QCD Lagrangian (or a controlled effective field theory thereof), establishing a quantitative and model-independent connection between the observed in-medium broadening of ρ_V and the temperature/density evolution of the chiral order parameters that signal chiral symmetry restoration. In particular, determine whether the melting of the ρ as seen in heavy-ion dilepton spectra implies, and is implied by, chiral restoration in the same medium, beyond the level of model-dependent conjectures.

Additionally, formulate and answer the following experimental-theoretical question: assuming forthcoming high-precision dilepton data in the low- and intermediate-mass regions from heavy-ion collisions at the LHC and RHIC, as well as small-system (pp, pA) collisions, can one decide whether the collective behavior observed in small collision systems is accompanied by the formation of a thermalized partonic medium of the same nature as that produced in large systems?
artifact.category_tag: QCD chiral symmetry and dilepton spectra
artifact.status_search_result: The theoretical connection between ρ-meson melting and chiral symmetry restoration remains an active research topic. Recent works (2021–2025), including studies using Weinberg-type sum rules, chiral effective theories, and inverse QCD sum rules, continue to refine the link but treat it as not yet rigorously derived from first principles. Likewise, the experimental program on intermediate-mass dileptons and small-system collectivity is still ongoing, with definitive determinations awaiting LHC/RHIC detector upgrades and analyses.

status_evidence.title: Effects of chiral symmetry restoration on meson and dilepton production in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the link between chiral restoration and dilepton/meson observables, indicating the connection is still being modeled rather than derived from first principles.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between in-medium ρ modifications and chiral restoration continues to be investigated via effective approaches as of 2021–2022.

status_evidence.title: Reappraisal of the rho meson in nuclear matter by the inverse QCD sum rules method
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) reanalysis of rho-meson properties in nuclear matter via inverse QCD sum rules, finding mass shift and broadening consistent with medium and baryon-resonance effects.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2025 work continues to refine, but does not definitively establish, the rigorous connection between ρ broadening and chiral order parameters.

status_evidence.title: Is Rho-Meson Melting Compatible with Chiral Restoration?
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier study showing compatibility of ρ melting with chiral restoration via Weinberg sum rules within model assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: The compatibility argument is established only at the level of model-dependent sum-rule analyses.
